chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is for the one who visits the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) purposely?' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'For him is Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the immense spiritual merit of Ziyarah, linking the physical act of visiting the Prophet’s grave with the ultimate reward of Paradise. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the enduring connection between the Imams and the Prophet, serving as a foundational text for the practice of pilgrimage to the Prophet’s shrine in Medina.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Najran who said,
‘I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What is for the one who, purposely, visits Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For him is the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn abu Najran who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’What is the reward for one who visits the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, voluntarily?’ He (the Imam) replied, ’The reward for him is paradise.’”
